fatal_errors: The proposed nanoflake incorporation does not reconstruct the target intervention of varying Mo content in a CoCrFeNiMox–Ni/MoS2–Ag–Cr2O3 composite.
Neither cited study supports effectiveness from cryogenic to high temperatures; E1 reports only ambient testing of a sprayed sulfide coating on steel.
E1 concerns a transition-metal-dichalcogenide HEA lubricant coating, not incorporation of metallic 2D HEA nanoflakes into an HEA component.
The claimed adaptive mechanism is undefined and does not identify temperature-dependent lubricant-film or oxide/molybdate-glaze formation.
No quantitative improvement, processing specification, tribological conditions, or credible service-temperature limits are provided.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general goal of lowering friction and wear in HEA-based moving components and supplies a basic treated-versus-untreated falsification test. However, it misses the paper's compositionally specific intervention, SPS processing, room-temperature-to-800 °C test conditions, Mo-induced lattice distortion and sigma-phase strengthening, and temperature-dependent MoS2/Ag and oxide–silver-molybdate tribofilms. Its evidence establishes promising ambient lubrication by sprayed high-entropy dichalcogenide flakes and low friction in a separate nanostructured HEA, but it does not validate incorporation into an HEA substrate or performance across the asserted cryogenic-to-high-temperature range. Thus it is an under-supported alternative rather than a reconstruction.
